objectives: Identify /k/ at the beginning and end of words.
Connect /k/ to c and k graphemes.
Contrast /k/ with previously learned consonants and short vowels.
concepts: Phonemes are heard before they are represented in print.
The /k/ sound can be represented by c or k in common words.
Sound position helps learners isolate a phoneme.

definitions.definition: The smallest unit of sound that can distinguish words.
A letter or letter group used to represent a sound.
The first sound heard in a spoken word.

workedExamples: kid → /k/ at the beginning, represented by k.
commonMistakes: Confusing /k/ with /t/ because both can occur at word edges.
Focusing on the letter name instead of the sound.
Missing /k/ at the end of a word.
Assuming c always represents the same sound in every context.
keyTakeaways: Connect sound to c or k.

application: Match /k/ sounds to c and k in controlled words.
higherOrderThinking: Compare words where the vowel changes but the initial /k/ stays constant.
mixedReview: Combine /k/ recognition with previously learned short-vowel words.

quickRevision: Hear /k/ → locate it → connect to c/k.
formulaOrFactBank: /k/ can be represented by c or k in common words
mistakeBasedRevision: If /k/ is confused with another sound, stretch the word and isolate its first phoneme.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat initial and final /k/ discrimination with fresh word sets.

activities.name: Sound sort
steps: Check the first or final sound.

activities.name: Sound-to-letter match
steps: Choose c or k from the word.

outcomes: Learner connects /k/ to c and k graphemes.
Learner compares the target sound with known phonemes.
